# bufio

Types from the Go package `bufio` (a library PocketBase builds on), as JavaScript sees them: they turn up as values of [PocketBase's types](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase) and of hook events.

## bufio.ReadWriter

Has everything <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader">Reader</a></code>, <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufiowriter">Writer</a></code> has.

## bufio.Reader

Reader implements buffering for an io.Reader object.
A new Reader is created by calling `NewReader` or `NewReaderSize`;
alternatively the zero value of a Reader may be used after calling [`Reader.reset`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader)
on it.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `size()` | <code>(): number</code> | Size returns the size of the underlying buffer in bytes. |
| `reset()` | <code>(r: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#ioreader">io.Reader</a>): void</code> | Reset discards any buffered data, resets all state, and switches the buffered reader to read from r. Calling Reset on the zero value of [`Reader`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) initializes the internal buffer to the default size. Calling b.Reset(b) (that is, resetting a [`Reader`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) to itself) does nothing. |
| `peek()` | <code>(n: number): string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> | Peek returns the next n bytes without advancing the reader. The bytes stop being valid at the next read call. If necessary, Peek will read more bytes into the buffer in order to make n bytes available. If Peek returns fewer than n bytes, it also returns an error explaining why the read is short. The error is `ErrBufferFull` if n is larger than b's buffer size. |
| `discard()` | <code>(n: number): number</code> | Discard skips the next n bytes, returning the number of bytes discarded. |
| `read()` | <code>(p: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;): number</code> | Read reads data into p. It returns the number of bytes read into p. The bytes are taken from at most one Read on the underlying [`Reader`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader), hence n may be less than len(p). To read exactly len(p) bytes, use io.ReadFull(b, p). If the underlying [`Reader`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) can return a non-zero count with io.EOF, then this Read method can do so as well; see the [`io.reader`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#ioreader) docs. |
| `readByte()` | <code>(): number</code> | ReadByte reads and returns a single byte. If no byte is available, returns an error. |
| `unreadByte()` | <code>(): void</code> | UnreadByte unreads the last byte. Only the most recently read byte can be unread. |
| `readRune()` | <code>(): [number, number]</code> | ReadRune reads a single UTF-8 encoded Unicode character and returns the rune and its size in bytes. If the encoded rune is invalid, it consumes one byte and returns unicode.ReplacementChar (U+FFFD) with a size of 1. |
| `unreadRune()` | <code>(): void</code> | UnreadRune unreads the last rune. If the most recent method called on the [`Reader`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) was not a [`Reader.readRune`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader), [`Reader.unreadRune`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) returns an error. (In this regard it is stricter than [`Reader.unreadByte`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader), which will unread the last byte from any read operation.) |
| `buffered()` | <code>(): number</code> | Buffered returns the number of bytes that can be read from the current buffer. |
| `readSlice()` | <code>(delim: number): string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> | ReadSlice reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a slice pointing at the bytes in the buffer. The bytes stop being valid at the next read. If ReadSlice encounters an error before finding a delimiter, it returns all the data in the buffer and the error itself (often io.EOF). ReadSlice fails with error `ErrBufferFull` if the buffer fills without a delim. Because the data returned from ReadSlice will be overwritten by the next I/O operation, most clients should use [`Reader.readBytes`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) or ReadString instead. ReadSlice returns err != nil if and only if line does not end in delim. |
| `readLine()` | <code>(): [string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;, boolean]</code> | ReadLine is a low-level line-reading primitive. Most callers should use [Reader.ReadBytes]('\n') or [Reader.ReadString]('\n') instead or use a `Scanner`. |
| `readBytes()` | <code>(delim: number): string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> | ReadBytes reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a slice containing the data up to and including the delimiter. If ReadBytes encounters an error before finding a delimiter, it returns the data read before the error and the error itself (often io.EOF). ReadBytes returns err != nil if and only if the returned data does not end in delim. For simple uses, a Scanner may be more convenient. |
| `readString()` | <code>(delim: number): string</code> | ReadString reads until the first occurrence of delim in the input, returning a string containing the data up to and including the delimiter. If ReadString encounters an error before finding a delimiter, it returns the data read before the error and the error itself (often io.EOF). ReadString returns err != nil if and only if the returned data does not end in delim. For simple uses, a Scanner may be more convenient. |
| `writeTo()` | <code>(w: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#iowriter">io.Writer</a>): number</code> | WriteTo implements io.WriterTo. This may make multiple calls to the [`Reader.read`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) method of the underlying [`Reader`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader). If the underlying reader supports the [`Reader.writeTo`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) method, this calls the underlying [`Reader.writeTo`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufioreader) without buffering. |

## bufio.Writer

Writer implements buffering for an [`io.writer`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#iowriter) object.
If an error occurs writing to a [`Writer`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufiowriter), no more data will be
accepted and all subsequent writes, and [`Writer.flush`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufiowriter), will return the error.
After all data has been written, the client should call the
[`Writer.flush`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufiowriter) method to guarantee all data has been forwarded to
the underlying [`io.writer`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#iowriter).

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `size()` | <code>(): number</code> | Size returns the size of the underlying buffer in bytes. |
| `reset()` | <code>(w: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#iowriter">io.Writer</a>): void</code> | Reset discards any unflushed buffered data, clears any error, and resets b to write its output to w. Calling Reset on the zero value of [`Writer`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufiowriter) initializes the internal buffer to the default size. Calling w.Reset(w) (that is, resetting a [`Writer`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufiowriter) to itself) does nothing. |
| `flush()` | <code>(): void</code> | Flush writes any buffered data to the underlying [`io.writer`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#iowriter). |
| `available()` | <code>(): number</code> | Available returns how many bytes are unused in the buffer. |
| `availableBuffer()` | <code>(): string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> | AvailableBuffer returns an empty buffer with b.Available() capacity. This buffer is intended to be appended to and passed to an immediately succeeding [`Writer.write`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/bufio#bufiowriter) call. The buffer is only valid until the next write operation on b. |
| `buffered()` | <code>(): number</code> | Buffered returns the number of bytes that have been written into the current buffer. |
| `write()` | <code>(p: string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;): number</code> | Write writes the contents of p into the buffer. It returns the number of bytes written. If nn < len(p), it also returns an error explaining why the write is short. |
| `writeByte()` | <code>(c: number): void</code> | WriteByte writes a single byte. |
| `writeRune()` | <code>(r: number): number</code> | WriteRune writes a single Unicode code point, returning the number of bytes written and any error. |
| `writeString()` | <code>(s: string): number</code> | WriteString writes a string. It returns the number of bytes written. If the count is less than len(s), it also returns an error explaining why the write is short. |
| `readFrom()` | <code>(r: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/io#ioreader">io.Reader</a>): number</code> | ReadFrom implements `io.readerFrom`. If the underlying writer supports the ReadFrom method, this calls the underlying ReadFrom. If there is buffered data and an underlying ReadFrom, this fills the buffer and writes it before calling ReadFrom. |
